notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS (customer engagement platform) evaluating Redwood for productionizing chat-based support assistant and semantic search/re-ranking across product docs and support articles.
- Started on Hosted API to validate prompts and response quality; now moving to Dedicated POC for throughput predictability and data isolation.

Business/requirements highlights:
- Workloads: high-concurrency chat for live agents (multi-turn), nightly reranking/embeddings refresh job.
- Performance targets: chat p95 latency <= 250ms (token streaming acceptable), sustained 120-200 conversational requests/sec at peak across their EU+NA regions.
- Cost sensitivity: wants to compare unit token cost between hosted and dedicated; target TCO reduction ~30% vs hosted at scale.
- Model preferences: open-models first (Llama2-70B variant, quantized), option to route to smaller variants for low-priority queries.
- Routing/availability: must support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to model variants / other region when capacity constrained. They explicitly asked for region-failover behavior between NA and EU.
- Rollback: require deterministic rollback plan and traceable request routing for incident RCA.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO via SAML, audit logs and KMS integration for key material, retention controls and EU data residency for EU customers.

Conversation snippets & quotes:
- "We liked the hosted quality — now we need predictable throughput and isolation for customer data" — VP Eng (Samir Iqbal).
- "Can we canary a new quantized model in EU only, then failover to NA small variant if our EU pool drops below 60% capacity?" — Lead Infra (Ava Chen).

POC plan (agreed in meeting):
- Week 0: Access & onboarding (VPC peering, SAML test account).
- Week 1: Baseline: replicate typical prompt set on hosted to capture latency/cost metrics.
- Week 2-3: Dedicated POC deploy (small pool) + enable continuous batching + KV prefix caching; run synthetic load and real production shadow traffic.
- Week 4: Canary rollout of quantized 70B variant to 5% traffic in EU region; monitor quality/regression and latency.
- Week 5: Expand canary to 25% if no regressions; run failover drill to NA small-variant, measure failover latency and request continuity.
- Week 6: Final evaluation — cost report, SLO attainment, security signoff.

Open questions / blockers we are tracking:
- Legal still has outstanding items on vendor DPA and EU data residency (security questionnaire sent 2026-03-05).
- Need detailed pricing for reserved capacity tiers + burst pricing during peak. Drive doc 'poc-dedicated-pricing' is linked.
- They want a simple runbook for canary rollback and automated policy to route to fallback variants during cold-start spikes.

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- SE Diego to provide recommended autoscaling policy: warm pools + burst to spare capacity; include metrics to trigger region-failover.
- Measure token-level cost with continuous-batching on vs off; get Redwood Optimize suggestions pre-POC to reduce tokens/cost.
- Track evaluation metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, QA score on a validation prompt set, failover recovery time.

Action items:
- Deliver Dedicated POC environment (Redwood) by 2026-03-15.
- SE to share canary rollout example config + fallback routing policy by 2026-03-14.
- AE to schedule procurement sync with Finance & Legal (Samir + CFO) next week.
